Hi guys, just joined Voat and thought I'd share my app that I published last week. Anyways, first things first, the catch(s):

  • Only for US and designed for Android Lollipop (although I just rolled out a compatibility update for KitKat). For those receiving the incompatibility message, make sure your phone is updated to the latest version (Go to the Settings Menu and click on 'About Phone')

  • Despite all the perfectly built budgeting apps out there, I wanted one that specifically catered to my own preferences. So what you guys see is an app that is designed around my own personal life, and may not necessarily be for you.

It's completely free (no ads, no in-app purchases, no collecting your data, I made this for myself and thought I'd give it a polish and share with the rest of the world) on the Play Store here: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.mushroomrobot.finwiz

And so without repeating the description in the link, here’s what led me to building my own app. In the past I've used YNAB and I have to say those guys have the whole budgeting process mastered. However I had a couple of personal issues with it, which actually is the foundation of why I built this app:

  • Completely mobile centered: Does not need a desktop counterpart or to connect to the cloud.

Let's face it, even coming from a finance background, who actually has time to sit down on a PC to reconcile their monthly budgets? Okay, I definitely do...but who actually is not lazy enough to do that?! Not this guy! This guy has so much laziness that he spent probably x10000 more time and energy creating a completely standalone app so he wouldn’t have to spend the 5 minutes required every month to complete said task. Also I’ll be honest here: I didn’t want to fork over the $60 after my free trial ended.

But I really wished YNAB allowed you full control on the Android app, from adjusting budgets to creating new categories, all on the go without having to wait until you got home to do it on their desktop version. And putting the self-deprecating jokes aside, I actually found myself wanting to make more budget optimizations throughout my day as I tracked my expenses, but wasn't able to with just the mobile app. I did however include an export to csv option for if I ever decided to be not lazy.

  • My own version of form and function: This is completely subjective and everyone has their own preferences on this. Companies tend to find the balance that most people are willing to accept.

Unfortunately for me, I'm weird so often times my version of balance and a company's do not match. At times I'm a visual guy so I need my charts, a quick overview one next to my overview of budgets, and then a dedicated section of nothing but charts on charts.

Other times I'm strictly functional. "OMG this app has a separate page to input the amount?!" That takes an extra .5 seconds out of my day at McDonald’s having to wait for the page to load while I also wait for my Double Cheeseburger with added Big Mac sauce and leaf lettuce (free LPT for you guys: The Ghetto Man's Big Mac, just $1.39. Also bonus LPT: Specifically request 'leaf lettuce', because just saying 'lettuce' results in the cheap shredded coleslaw kind. No one likes that kind). Thus I simplified the recording expenses process (the main part of utilizing a budgeting app!) down to where it just only displays exactly what it needs to later provide you with the data necessary to analyze and improve on your spending, and also ensuring you spend the least amount of time entering an expense.

TLDR: I made a budgeting app. It’s probably not better than the ones currently out there. It does however cater to my own taste and it's free, so at least I got that going for me.
